scenarios.text: A floor conduit cell in a powered workshop run is destroyed by a grenade. A constructor picks up steel, carries it to the blueprint placed on that destroyed cell, and on the way steps onto the sparking loose end beside it; then builds the conduit. The game shows no shock on the constructor.
scenarios.expect: accept: the constructor carrying material to or building the conduit that joins this end is safe, delivery step included

scenarios.text: A floor conduit cell is destroyed, leaving a sparking live end. A different constructor, building an unrelated conduit blueprint across the room, is routed across that sparking end cell. The game shows him walk through with no shock and no damage.
scenarios.expect: reject: only the constructor whose job joins this end is exempt; a constructor on some other conduit is shocked like any crosser

scenarios.text: The player turns off the overhead-lines master in Mod Settings, leaving the shock setting at All. A hauler then crosses the sparking live end of a cut floor cord. The game shows no shock.
scenarios.expect: reject: turning off overhead lines does not silence floor ends; floor-end shock must not be gated on the aerial master

scenarios.text: On a fresh install the player opens Mod Settings and finds the shock choice set to Only downed lines. He switches it to All and, without restarting, a hauler crossing a live floor-cord end is shocked.
scenarios.expect: reject: the default on a fresh settings file must be All

scenarios.text: With the shock setting on Only downed lines, a FlowWorks bridge deck collapses and drops a powered cord. A hauler crosses that dropped cord and is shocked; a second hauler crossing a sparking cut floor-cord end is not shocked.
scenarios.expect: accept: Only downed lines keeps FlowWorks' dropped deck cords biting and spares floor ends

scenarios.text: A live overhead span falls after a mast is killed, and a colonist taking the re-string job for a different, distant span is routed across this wire's sparking end. He is not shocked; a hauler crossing the same spot a moment later is.
scenarios.expect: reject: the exemption is keyed on the wire the job targets, not the job type; a re-stringer of a different span is shocked

scenarios.text: A chemfuel puddle sits on the sparking live end cell of a cut floor cord; fallen-wire ignition is on and shock reach is All. Time passes; the puddle never catches fire. Elsewhere a puddle under the sparking end of a live fallen overhead wire bursts into flame.
scenarios.expect: accept: a live fallen wire lights fuel, and the ignition sweep is not widened to floor-cord ends

scenarios.text: A powered line runs from a generator through conduit to a lamp, and a battery holding charge sits on the far side beyond the lamp. A middle conduit cell is destroyed. The game shows two loose ends with nothing across the gap, and both ends spark.
scenarios.expect: accept: each side still reaches its own power source, so both ends sparking is right

scenarios.text: A generator feeds a run of conduit to a lamp, with no other source. A middle cell is destroyed: the near end sparks and the far end lies limp. The player switches the generator off; a minute later the near end is still sparking.
scenarios.expect: reject: an end that has lost its last power source must go dead within a few seconds; an end cut off from all power that sparks is wrong

scenarios.text: A water pump is fed by conduit laid in the next cell, not under it. The game draws one cord from the conduit to the pump, entering its footprint on a diagonal and sliding underneath, and also a second short cable at the pump that runs to nothing.
scenarios.expect: reject: no phantom second cable at an adjacent-fed pump

scenarios.text: Three of our powered masts stand in a line, the middle one spanned to both others, and a fourth mast of ours is spanned to the first. Another faction claims the middle mast. The game shows both wires to the middle mast taken down and coiled with a message, while the span between the first and fourth masts also drops.
scenarios.expect: reject: only wires between poles of different owners come down; the same-owner span must stay up and powered

scenarios.text: The player turns off the FlowWorks pipe-pole switch while the GSS master is on. Pipe poles change back, and the power masts in the yard also lose their styled look and revert to vanilla.
scenarios.expect: reject: the pipe-pole switch has its own scope and leaves power poles alone

scenarios.text: In one session the player plays a game with a clamped tap on a neighbour's line, quits to menu, and loads a different save that has no tap. Over the next two days, goodwill with that neighbour in the loaded game falls steadily though no tap exists on the map.
scenarios.expect: reject: nothing of one game, no tap included, carries into the next game loaded in the same session

scenarios.text: The player clamps a power tap onto a neighbour's line and power flows one way into the colony. A neighbour pawn sees the clamp; goodwill with that neighbour drops steadily each day, and goodwill with an unrelated third faction drops by the same amount over the same days.
scenarios.expect: reject: the drain must hit only the victim faction; every other faction's goodwill stays unchanged

scenarios.text: In the Modern look, a conduit 3-way junction sits in the middle of a workshop floor. The game draws a small splitter box on the junction cell, and the three cords at that junction each plug into it.
scenarios.expect: reject: the Modern look draws the long power strip at junctions, never the splitter box

scenarios.text: Conduit runs into a fully enclosed rock pocket that no cord can route around. The cord ends at a plate on the near face of the rock, and reappears from a matching plate on the far face; no part of it is drawn over the rock.
scenarios.expect: accept: an unroutable cord dives under a barrier with a plate on each side and is never drawn across rock

scenarios.text: Mod Settings has the most-sparking-ends limit set to 1 and shock reach on All. Two floor runs are each cut, leaving two powered loose ends on the map. Only one of them draws sparks; the other lies still. A hauler's path crosses the end cell that is not sparking and he walks over it with no shock, while another hauler crossing the sparking end is shocked.
scenarios.expect: reject: an end bites while it is live even when the spark limit leaves it unsparked; shock keyed on the drawn spark set is a named false pass

scenarios.text: A floor run is cut and its fed end sparks. A constructor assigned to build a conduit blueprint in another room, unrelated to the cut, is routed straight across the sparking end cell and walks on unharmed. A hauler crossing the same cell a minute later is shocked.
scenarios.expect: reject: only the constructor whose job targets the conduit joining this end is safe; a constructor building some other conduit must be shocked (no 'every constructor safe')

scenarios.text: Shock reach is set to Only downed lines. A hauler crosses a live floor-cord end and is not shocked. A second hauler crosses the live fallen wire under a killed mast and is shocked. A third crosses the powered cord dropped by a collapsed FlowWorks bridge deck and is not shocked.
scenarios.expect: reject: under Only downed lines the FlowWorks dropped deck cord must still bite alongside the fallen wire

scenarios.text: Shock reach is All and the fallen-wire ignition switch is on. A chemfuel puddle lies on the sparking live end cell of a cut floor cord with nothing else burning nearby. After a short wait the puddle catches fire.
scenarios.expect: reject: the ignition sweep is not widened to floor ends; fuel under a cut floor cord's live end must not light

scenarios.text: A conduit line has a generator at one end and a charged battery at the other. A middle cell is destroyed. Both loose ends spark, no cord is drawn across the gap. When only the generator is switched off, within a few seconds the generator-side end goes limp and the battery-side end keeps sparking.
scenarios.expect: accept: each end sparks exactly while its side still reaches a source; both sparking with a source on each side is stated as right

scenarios.text: Two overhead spans are down. A colonist takes the re-string job for the far span and is routed across the sparking end of the nearer fallen live wire; he walks over it unharmed. The colonist assigned to re-string the nearer wire also reaches it unharmed.
scenarios.expect: reject: the exemption is keyed on the wire the job targets, not on the re-string job type; the colonist re-stringing a different span must be shocked

scenarios.text: The player turns the overhead-lines master switch off in Mod Settings, leaving shock reach on All. A hauler then crosses the sparking live end of a cut floor cord and is not shocked. With the overhead master back on, the same crossing shocks him.
scenarios.expect: reject: turning overhead lines off must not silence floor ends; floor-end shock gated on the aerial master is a named false pass

scenarios.text: A conduit cell in a powered floor run is destroyed and a rebuild blueprint is placed on it. The constructor assigned to it carries steel to the blueprint, stepping on the sparking end cell on the way, and is shocked. Later, while actually building the frame on that cell, he is not shocked.
scenarios.expect: reject: safety covers carrying material to as well as building the conduit that joins this end; an exemption covering only the building step is a named false pass

e1.why: Constructor carrying steel to or building the conduit that joins this end is safe.

e2.why: A constructor on an unrelated conduit job crossing a live end must be shocked.

e3.why: Turning overhead lines off does not silence floor ends; under All the hauler is shocked.

e4.why: Default on a fresh install must be All, not Only downed lines.

e5.why: Only downed lines keeps dropped deck cords biting and floor ends silent.

e6.why: Re-stringer of a different span crossing this live wire must be shocked.

e7.why: Ignition is not widened to floor ends; live fallen wire lights fuel.

e8.why: Each side has its own source (generator, charged battery), so both ends spark.

e9.why: An end cut off from all power must stop sparking within one 250-tick poll.

e10.why: No phantom second cable at an adjacent-fed pump.

e11.why: Wires between poles of one owner stay up; first-fourth span must not drop.

e12.why: Pipe-pole switch must leave power poles alone.

e13.why: No tap from a previous game may carry over and drain goodwill.

e14.why: Drain must hit only the victim faction; third faction goodwill unchanged.

e15.why: Modern draws the long power strip; a splitter box at junctions is red.

e16.why: Unroutable cord dives under the barrier with a plate on each face, none drawn over rock.

c2.why: Unrelated constructor crossing a live end must be shocked; exemption only for joining conduit.

c3.why: Under Only downed lines the FlowWorks dropped deck cord must still shock.

c4.why: Fuel under a cut floor-cord end must not ignite; ignition is not widened.

c7.why: Floor-end shock must not be gated on the overhead master.

c8.why: Carrying steel to the joining blueprint is also safe; only-building exemption is a false pass.
